mainTopic: How many sets of lashes for eating one piece that carries several prohibitions: אבר מן החי, טרפה and חלב
overview: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about someone who eats an אבר מן החי from an animal that is a טרפה. רבי יוחנן says he gets lashes twice, and ריש לקיש says only once. רב יוסף explains that everyone agrees to two sets of lashes when the limb and the טרפה meat come from two different animals. The argument is only about one animal. The גמרא then gives several ways to explain that argument. אביי sets it at an animal that became a טרפה at birth. Two more explanations turn it into a question of whether a later prohibition can take effect on one that is already there. רבא sets it at a limb whose tearing off made the animal a טרפה. Next comes a dispute over רבי יוחנן's ruling about eating חלב from a living טרפה: is it two sets of lashes or three? The same kinds of explanations appear again, including a proof from the פסוק that lets נבלה and טרפה take effect on חלב. The other side's answer, that חלב is different because it has permitted cases, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute over a limb from a living טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says someone who eats an אבר מן החי from a טרפה is liable twice. ריש לקיש says he is liable only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ate a limb from a living animal that is a טרפה: רבי יוחנן says he is liable twice, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש says he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about one bite that breaks two prohibitions at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one piece of meat is both an אבר מן החי and meat from a טרפה. רבי יוחנן counts two separate sins, so the person gets two sets of lashes. ריש לקיש says only one prohibition takes effect, so he gets only one set.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut from an animal while it is still alive, which is forbidden to eat
An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat
Liable twice (two sets of lashes)
He is liable only once

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי מִן הַטְּרֵפָה,
phrases.english: If one ate a limb from a living animal, from a tereifa,
phrases.notes: One limb, cut off while the animal was alive, from an animal that is also a טרפה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: He is liable twice,
and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
He is liable only once.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי מִן הַטְּרֵפָה, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: two sets of lashes. ריש לקיש: one set of lashes.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's view seems difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן's view fits well, but ריש לקיש's view is a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי יוחנן it works out well. But according to רבי שמעון בן לקיש it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש, saying his view does not fit what was taught earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source taught just before this treats אבר מן החי and meat from a טרפה as two separate prohibitions, each from its own פסוק. Two separate prohibitions should mean two sets of lashes, as רבי יוחנן says. So how can ריש לקיש say only one?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense
It works out well
It is difficult (a challenge)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan it works out well,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ קַשְׁיָא.
phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish it is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one side of the dispute in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling of only one set of lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier source counts two separate prohibitions, which should mean two sets of lashes.

steps.title: רב יוסף: one animal versus two animals
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the earlier source spoke about two animals, where everyone agrees the person is liable twice. The argument is only about one animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about one animal, and there about two animals. With two animals he is liable twice. With one animal they argue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends ריש לקיש by narrowing the case: the earlier source was about two different animals, and the argument is only about one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the limb came from one living animal and the טרפה meat came from a different animal, these are clearly two separate sins, and even ריש לקיש agrees he gets two sets of lashes. The argument is only about one piece from one animal that is both an אבר מן החי and a טרפה. So the earlier source does not contradict ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the opening of an answer)
Here... there: splitting two sources into two different cases
An animal
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Even ריש לקיש agrees to two sets of lashes in the case of two animals. He only says 'one' when a single piece from one animal carries both prohibitions.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult,
here it is about one animal,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: there it is about two animals.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the earlier source that counted two prohibitions.

phrases.english: With two animals, he is liable twice,
with one animal, they argue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בִּבְהֵמָה אַחַת, כָּאן בִּשְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one animal versus two animals)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the earlier source and the dispute were about the same case, so ריש לקיש contradicted it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is about two animals, where all agree to two sets of lashes. The dispute is only about one animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the next question: what exactly is the one-animal case they argue about?

steps.title: What exactly is the one-animal case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case of one animal רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of one animal, about what do they argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case behind the argument. This question sets up אביי's answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an animal becomes a טרפה at some point either before or after birth, so one prohibition would come first. The גמרא wants to know the precise case where the two sides would really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: In what? (about which case)
In the case of a single animal

phrases.english: With one animal, about what do they argue?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּבְהֵמָה אַחַת, בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the one-animal case named in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case of one animal where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree

steps.title: אביי: it became a טרפה at the moment of birth, and רבי יוחנן's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case is an animal that became a טרפה just as most of it came out of its mother. רבי יוחנן holds that each limb counts as its own unit from birth, so both prohibitions arrive together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For example, where it became a טרפה as most of it came out at birth. One Sage (רבי יוחנן) holds: an animal, even while alive, stands to be divided into limbs, and the prohibition of טרפה and the prohibition of a limb come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the exact case they argue about, then starts explaining רבי יוחנן's reason for saying two sets of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal counts as born when most of it comes out, and that is when אבר מן החי first applies. Here it became a טרפה at that same moment, so neither prohibition came first. רבי יוחנן says each limb is already treated as its own unit, so both prohibitions take hold at once and both count. ריש לקיש's side comes next in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / such as
It became a טרפה
Most of it coming out (the moment of birth)
One Sage holds
It stands to be divided into limbs, so each limb counts as its own unit
Together, at the same time

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's explanation, the dispute is about one animal that became a טרפה at the very moment of birth. רבי יוחנן says both prohibitions arrive together, so the person is liable twice. Later steps give other ways to explain the dispute.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּטְרְפָה עִם יְצִיאַת רוּבָּהּ,
phrases.english: Abaye said: For example, where it became a tereifa as the majority of it emerged,
phrases.notes: As most of the newborn animal came out of its mother's womb, which counts as being born.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: an animal, during its life,
stands to be divided into limbs,
and the prohibition of tereifa and the prohibition of a limb
come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּטְרְפָה עִם יְצִיאַת רוּבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4 and begins explaining רבי יוחנן's side
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is an animal that became a טרפה at the moment of birth. רבי יוחנן holds that each limb is its own unit, so both prohibitions arrive together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, both prohibitions take effect at the same moment, so the person is liable twice.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's side: limbs are not separate units, so the limb prohibition comes too late
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that a living animal's limbs are not separate units. So the איסור אבר מן החי only starts later, and it cannot take effect on the איסור טרפה that is already there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage (ריש לקיש) holds that while an animal is alive, it does not count as made up of separate limbs. So the prohibition of a limb from a living animal does not come and take effect on top of the prohibition of טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer by explaining why ריש לקיש says the person is liable only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's case, the animal became a טרפה right at birth, so the איסור טרפה is there from the start. According to ריש לקיש, the איסור אבר מן החי only begins when a limb is actually cut off. By then the איסור טרפה is already in place, and the later prohibition cannot be added on top of it, so there is only one punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal while it is still alive
It does not count as standing to be divided into separate limbs
The prohibition of eating a limb taken from a living animal (אבר מן החי)
The prohibition of eating an animal with a fatal injury or defect
Takes effect, lands on

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This Sage is ריש לקיש, who said the person is liable only once.

phrases.english: an animal during its life does not stand as separate limbs,
and the prohibition of a limb does not come
and take effect on the prohibition of טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר, בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לָאו לְאֵבָרִים עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from step 5 by giving ריש לקיש's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש holds limbs are not units during the animal's life, so the limb prohibition arrives after the טרפה prohibition and cannot take effect on it.

steps.title: Second explanation: both agree on limbs, and they argue whether the limb prohibition can land on the טרפה prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a living animal's limbs are not separate units. The argument is whether the later איסור אבר can still take effect on the איסור טרפה that came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that everyone agrees that an animal during its life does not count as separate limbs. They argue about whether the limb prohibition takes effect on top of the טרפה prohibition. One Sage holds it does come and take effect, and the other Sage holds it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain the same argument from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sides agree on the order of events: the איסור טרפה comes first and the איסור אבר comes later. The argument has moved to a new question: can a second prohibition take effect on food that is already forbidden? רבי יוחנן says yes, so the person is liable twice. ריש לקיש says no, so he is liable once.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say instead. This introduces another possible explanation.
Everyone, meaning both sides agree on this point
They argue, they disagree
Whether a new prohibition can take effect on something that is already forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides now agree that limbs are NOT separate units. That point is no longer the argument. The argument is only whether a second prohibition can be added on top of the first.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say that everyone agrees
an animal during its life does not stand as separate limbs,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמֵיתֵי אִיסּוּר אֵבֶר מֵיחַל אַאִיסּוּר טְרֵפָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי:
phrases.english: and they argue about whether the limb prohibition comes to take effect on the טרפה prohibition:
One Sage holds that the limb prohibition comes
phrases.notes: This first Sage is רבי יוחנן, who said liable twice.

phrases.english: and takes effect on the טרפה prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לָא אָתֵי אִיסּוּר אֵבֶר
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that the limb prohibition does not come
and take effect on the טרפה prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לָאו לְאֵבָרִים עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's explanation (steps 5-6) with another reason for the same argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both agree limbs are not units during life. They argue whether the later limb prohibition can take effect on the existing טרפה prohibition.

steps.title: Third explanation: both agree limbs are units, and they argue whether the טרפה prohibition can land on the limb prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a living animal's limbs are separate units from birth, so the איסור אבר is there first. The animal became a טרפה later, and they argue whether the איסור טרפה can take effect on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that everyone agrees that an animal during its life does count as separate limbs. The case is where it became a טרפה afterward, and they argue whether the טרפה prohibition takes effect on top of the limb prohibition. One Sage holds it comes and takes effect, and the other Sage holds it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to explain the argument, this time with the order of the two prohibitions flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the איסור אבר is already in place from birth, because the limbs count as units. The איסור טרפה only comes later, when the animal is injured after birth. The question is the same as before, whether a second prohibition can be added, but now the טרפה prohibition is the one coming second.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a טרפה
Afterward, here meaning after the animal was born
Comes and takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to explain the argument. (1) אביי: they argue whether limbs are units from birth. (2) Both say limbs are not units, so טרפה comes first; they argue whether the limb prohibition can be added. (3) Both say limbs are units, so the limb prohibition comes first; they argue whether טרפה can be added. In every version, רבי יוחנן says liable twice and ריש לקיש says liable once.

phrases.english: If you wish, say that everyone agrees
an animal during its life stands as separate limbs,
and the case is where it became a טרפה afterward,
phrases.notes: Afterward means after it was born, so the limb prohibition was already there.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמֵיתֵי אִיסּוּר טְרֵפָה חָיֵיל אַאִיסּוּר אֵבֶר קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and they argue about whether the טרפה prohibition comes and takes effect on the limb prohibition.
One Sage holds it comes and takes effect,
and the other Sage holds it does not come and take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לְאֵבָרִים עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third explanation, the mirror image of step 7, with the limb prohibition coming first and טרפה second.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both agree limbs are units from birth. The animal became a טרפה later, and they argue whether the טרפה prohibition can take effect on the existing limb prohibition.

steps.title: רבא's case: tearing off a limb makes the animal a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the argument is about a case where someone tore a limb off an animal, and that tearing made the animal a טרפה. רבי יוחנן holds that a living animal's limbs are not separate units, so איסור אבר and איסור טרפה come at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where he tore a limb off the animal and made it a טרפה through that limb. One Sage (רבי יוחנן) holds that a living animal does not count as separate limbs, so the limb prohibition and the טרפה prohibition come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the question of which case רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about. Here he explains רבי יוחנן's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing off the limb does two things at once: it creates a torn-off limb, and it damages the animal so that it becomes a טרפה. רבי יוחנן holds that the limb was not a separate unit while attached, so its איסור אבר מן החי only starts when it is torn. That is the very moment the animal becomes a טרפה, so both prohibitions arrive together and both count.

keyTerms.meaning: Tore off or plucked off
And made it a טרפה through it (through tearing off that limb)
While alive, an animal's limbs are not treated as separate units
They come together, at the same moment

steps.confusionAlert: Careful! In אביי's version (Step 5), רבי יוחנן held that limbs ARE separate units from birth. In רבא's version, רבי יוחנן holds the opposite: they are NOT separate units. Both versions end with רבי יוחנן saying the prohibitions come together, but the reasoning is flipped.

phrases.english: Rava says:
For example, where he tore a limb off it
and made it a tereifa through it.
phrases.notes: Losing that limb is itself the damage that makes the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: One Sage holds:
an animal during its life does not stand as separate limbs,
so the prohibition of a limb and the prohibition of a tereifa
come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁתָּלַשׁ מִמֶּנָּה אֵבֶר וּטְרָפָהּ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new case to replace אביי's case for the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a limb torn off that makes the animal a טרפה. According to רבי יוחנן, limbs are not separate while alive, so both prohibitions start together.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's side in רבא's version
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that a living animal's limbs are separate units from birth. So the limb was already forbidden as אבר מן החי, and the later טרפה prohibition cannot take effect on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other Sage (ריש לקיש) holds that a living animal does count as separate limbs, so the טרפה prohibition cannot come and take effect on the limb prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by giving ריש לקיש's side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each limb is its own unit from birth, the איסור אבר מן החי was already on the limb long before the tearing. When the tearing makes the animal a טרפה, that is a new prohibition coming onto something that is already forbidden. ריש לקיש holds it cannot take hold, so there is only one prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: While alive, an animal's limbs already count as separate units
Takes effect, takes hold
A prohibition taking effect on something already forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's version: רבי יוחנן says limbs are NOT separate while alive, so both prohibitions come together. ריש לקיש says they ARE separate, so the אבר prohibition came first and blocks the טרפה prohibition.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds:
an animal during its life does stand as separate limbs,
and the prohibition of a tereifa does not come
and take effect on the prohibition of a limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר, בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לְאֵבָרִים עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation by giving the opposing side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to ריש לקיש, the איסור אבר was there from birth, so the later איסור טרפה cannot take effect.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: eating חלב from a living טרפה gets two sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן ruled: someone who eats חלב from a living animal that is a טרפה gets lashes twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone ate forbidden fat from a living animal that is a טרפה, he is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן about one piece of food with several prohibitions on it. This is the version of רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three prohibitions could apply here: חלב, אבר מן החי, and טרפה. This report counts only two of them. The גמרא will soon ask which reasoning stands behind 'two' versus 'three'.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of a kosher domestic animal
From a living animal
Liable twice (two sets of lashes)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says
that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל חֵלֶב מִן הַחַי מִן הַטְּרֵפָה –
phrases.english: If one ate forbidden fat from a living animal that is a tereifa,
he is liable to two sets of lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related teaching about several prohibitions landing on one piece of food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating חלב from a living טרפה makes one liable to two sets of lashes.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the report should say three
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי tells רבי חייא בר אבא that he should report רבי יוחנן's ruling as three sets of lashes, because that is how רבי אמי holds the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: Let the Master say three, because I say three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes back on the report he just heard. He says רבי יוחנן's ruling should be three sets of lashes, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a dispute about what רבי יוחנן actually said. רבי אמי holds that all three prohibitions take effect: חלב, אבר מן החי, and טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: But let the Master say (a polite way to suggest a correction)
Three (sets of lashes)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
But let the Master say three,
because I say three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי: וְלֵימָא מָר שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number given in רבי חייא בר אבא's report.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר אבא's report that the eater gets two sets of lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אמי holds that the correct ruling counts all three prohibitions, so the eater gets three sets of lashes.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's report also says three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another report, from רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן. It says the eater gets three sets of lashes, which supports רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone ate חלב from a living animal that is a טרפה, he is liable three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אמי is not alone. Another student, רבי אבהו, also reported 'three' in רבי יוחנן's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two clear versions of רבי יוחנן's ruling: two lashes (רבי חייא בר אבא) or three lashes (רבי אמי and רבי אבהו). That sets up the question of what reasoning lies behind each version.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable three times: for חלב, for אבר מן החי, and for טרפה
From an animal that is a טרפה

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל חֵלֶב מִן הַחַי מִן הַטְּרֵפָה –
phrases.english: If one ate forbidden fat from a living animal that is a tereifa,
he is liable to three sets of lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אמי's version with an independent report.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן ruled three sets of lashes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבהו's report in the name of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: What do the two versions disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning lies behind the 'two' and 'three' versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what principle splits the two versions. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to find the exact case and the exact idea that leads one version to count two prohibitions and the other to count three.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two reports just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle and what case explain the 'two' versus 'three' versions of רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: Why three: all three prohibitions arrive at birth
steps.stepSummary: The case is an animal that became a טרפה as most of it came out of its mother. The 'three' side holds that a living animal's limbs are separate units, so איסור חלב, איסור אבר, and איסור טרפה all come at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where the animal became a טרפה just as most of it came out. The one who says three holds that a living animal does count as separate limbs, so the prohibitions of חלב, limb, and טרפה all come together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by setting the case at the moment of birth. It explains the reasoning of the side that says three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal becomes forbidden as soon as most of it is born, and in this case it also became a טרפה at that same moment. If its limbs already count as separate units, then איסור אבר מן החי also starts right then. The חלב prohibition starts then as well, so all three arrive together and all three count.

keyTerms.meaning: The coming out of most of the animal (being born)
Became a טרפה
The one who says (the opinion that holds)
The prohibition of eating forbidden fat

steps.whatToRemember: The 'three' version works because everything happens at birth. Limbs count as separate units, and the animal became a טרפה right then, so חלב, אבר מן החי, and טרפה all start together.

phrases.english: For example, where it became a tereifa as the majority of it emerged.
The one who said three holds:
an animal during its life does stand as separate limbs,
so that the prohibition of fat, and the prohibition of a limb,
and the prohibition of a tereifa come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּטְרְפָה עִם יְצִיאַת רוּבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving the case and explaining the 'three' opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a טרפה at birth. The 'three' side holds that limbs are separate units from birth, so all three prohibitions arrive together.

steps.title: The reasoning of the 'two lashes' side
steps.stepSummary: The 'two' side holds that a living animal's limbs are not separate units. So only איסור חלב and איסור טרפה apply, and איסור אבר מן החי cannot take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said 'two' holds that while an animal is alive, its limbs are not treated as separate units. So the איסור of חלב and the איסור of טרפה are both there, but the איסור of a limb cannot come and take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its first answer by explaining the 'two lashes' side, the mirror image of the 'three' side from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the limbs are not separate units, the איסור of a limb from a living animal does not start at the same moment as the other two. It comes later, when there are already other איסורים on the meat, so it cannot take hold. That leaves only two איסורים, which means two sets of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands as separate limbs, meaning each limb counts as its own unit while the animal is alive
A limb from a living animal, which is forbidden to eat
Comes and takes effect, said of an איסור landing on something
The general rule that a new איסור cannot take effect on something already forbidden

phrases.english: And the one who said two sets of lashes
holds that an animal, during its life,
does not stand as separate limbs,
so the prohibition of forbidden fat and the prohibition of a טרפה are there,
phrases.notes: These two started at the same moment, so both of them count.

phrases.english: but the prohibition of a limb does not come and take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁתַּיִם, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 15's answer by giving the opposite side's reasoning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Limbs of a living animal are not separate units, so איסור אבר comes later and cannot take effect on top of איסור חלב and איסור טרפה

steps.title: Second explanation: they argue whether the limb prohibition can land on top
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that a living animal's limbs are not separate units. They disagree about whether איסור אבר מן החי can take effect on top of the existing איסור חלב and איסור טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say that everyone agrees a living animal's limbs are not separate units. They argue about whether the איסור of a limb comes and takes effect on top of the איסור of חלב and the איסור of טרפה. One side says it does, and the other says it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain the same dispute. Now both sides agree on the facts and argue about a rule instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first explanation, the argument was about the facts: are the limbs separate units or not? Here everyone agrees the limb איסור comes second. The only question is whether this later איסור can still take hold. The 'three' side says yes, and the 'two' side says no.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say; this opens another possible explanation
Everyone agrees
They disagree about

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. It is a second way of explaining the same 'two versus three' dispute, so the reason for the argument has moved.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say instead
that everyone agrees that an animal during its life
does not stand as separate limbs,
and about whether the prohibition of a limb comes and takes effect

phrases.aramaic: אַאִיסּוּר חֵלֶב וְאַאִיסּוּר טְרֵפָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: on top of the prohibition of fat and the prohibition of a טרפה, they disagree.
One master holds it comes and takes effect,
and the other master holds it does not come and take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לָאו לְאֵבָרִים עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the same dispute that replaces the one in steps 15-16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two sides argue about whether a later איסור אבר can take effect on top of existing איסורים

steps.title: Third explanation: they argue whether a later טרפה prohibition can land on the limb prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree the limbs are separate units, and the animal became a טרפה only later. They disagree about whether the later איסור טרפה can take effect on top of the existing איסור אבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say that everyone agrees a living animal's limbs are separate units. The case is one where it became a טרפה later. They argue about whether the איסור of טרפה can take effect on top of the איסור of a limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to explain the dispute, this time with a slightly different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the limb איסור and the חלב איסור were in place from birth. The טרפה איסור comes afterward. So now the question is whether the late איסור of טרפה can take hold on top of the איסור of a limb.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a טרפה afterward, meaning after it was born
To take effect

steps.confusionAlert: In this explanation the order is reversed: the limb איסור comes first and the טרפה איסור comes last. It is the טרפה איסור that is in question now.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say instead
that everyone agrees that an animal during its life
stands as separate limbs,
and the case is where it became a טרפה afterward,
phrases.notes: So the limb and fat prohibitions were already in place before it became a טרפה.

phrases.english: and about whether the prohibition of a טרפה comes to take effect
on top of the prohibition of a limb, they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לְאֵבָרִים עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the dispute that changes both the assumption about the limbs and the timing of the טרפה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two sides argue about whether a later איסור טרפה takes effect on top of an existing איסור אבר

steps.title: The 'three' side learns from the case of חלב
steps.stepSummary: The 'three' side says the טרפה איסור does take effect, just as the תורה lets the איסורים of נבלה and טרפה take effect on top of an existing איסור חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One side holds that it does take effect, just like with חלב. As the master said, the תורה said: let the איסור of נבלה come and take effect on the איסור of חלב, and let the איסור of טרפה come and take effect on the איסור of חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the 'three' side of the third explanation by pointing to a source about חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a new איסור cannot land on something that is already forbidden. But a פסוק shows that the איסורים of נבלה and טרפה do land on חלב, which was forbidden first. The 'three' side says a later טרפה איסור can likewise land on the existing limb איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like the case of; this introduces a comparison
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
The תורה said; this shows that a rule comes straight from a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule 'one איסור cannot land on another' has exceptions the תורה itself makes. The dispute depends on whether those exceptions stretch to other cases.

phrases.english: One master holds: it comes and takes effect,
just as it is with forbidden fat,
as the master said: The תורה said

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא אִיסּוּר נְבֵלָה יָחוּל עַל אִיסּוּר חֵלֶב,
phrases.english: let the prohibition of a נבלה come and take effect on the prohibition of fat,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָבֹא אִיסּוּר טְרֵפָה יָחוּל עַל אִיסּוּר חֵלֶב.
phrases.english: and let the prohibition of a טרפה come and take effect on the prohibition of fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: אָתֵי חָיֵיל, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַחֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the 'three' side of the third explanation
steps.raayaObject: That a later איסור טרפה takes effect on top of an existing איסור אבר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching on ויקרא 7:24 that the איסורים of נבלה and טרפה take effect on top of איסור חלב

steps.title: The other side says חלב is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The 'two' side rejects the proof from חלב. איסור טרפה can take effect on top of חלב only because חלב has permitted exceptions. אבר מן החי may not have that feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side says: it is only for חלב that one is liable for the extra איסור, because it was permitted (in some situations).
steps.whatsHappening: The other side (the 'two' view) answers the proof from step 19. He says the case of חלב is different, so it proves nothing about אבר מן החי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 argued that if טרפה can take effect on top of חלב, it can also take effect on top of אבר מן החי. The answer is that חלב is weaker, because it has permitted exceptions, and that is why another איסור can take effect on it. אבר מן החי may have no such exceptions, so the later איסור טרפה cannot take effect on it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: the other side of the argument (here, the 'two' view)
Liable: he gets punished for that איסור
Was permitted: the איסור has situations where it is allowed
One איסור taking effect on top of another one that already exists

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the other side is saying חלב is permitted. חלב is fully forbidden. He only means it has some permitted exceptions, and that weakness lets a second איסור take effect on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general idea used often in the גמרא: an איסור that has permitted exceptions can have a second איסור take effect on it more easily.

phrases.english: And the other one [says]:
phrases.notes: This is the 'two' side, who answers the proof just brought by the 'three' side.

phrases.english: it is [only] for חלב that one is liable [for the extra איסור],
because it was permitted
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next עמוד, which explains when חלב is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, אַחֵלֶב הוּא דְּחַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 19 by pointing out that the source case (חלב) has a special feature.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison between חלב and אבר מן החי. It does not reject the rule that נבלה and טרפה take effect on חלב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חלב has permitted exceptions, which allow a second איסור to take effect on it. Without such a feature, אבר מן החי cannot be compared to it.
